text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Namibian officials are studying the impact of an electrified fence Botswana is erecting along their common border south of the West Caprivi game park. The fence is intended to prevent the cross-border spread of cattle diseases, but is said to be disrupting the lifestyle of migrant local populations and the movement of wilds.
- A labour consultancy has urged Gold Fields South Africa to inform its employees about its future plans for three Namibian mines run as Tsumeb Corp Ltd.
- Deputy Prisons Minister Michaela Hubschle says prison services are stretched to the limit.
- The opposition DTA party slammed President Sam Nujoma for accepting a new luxury limousine, which cost taxpayers N$3.4 million.
- Three Himba people from Kaokoland have left for a European tour to highlight opposition to the proposed Epupa hydro- electric scheme.
- The government has failed to answer questions about the distribution of N$36 million earmarked for former fighters in the war over South African rule.
